item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Jake Bauers put his team’s determination on full display, getting the Milwaukee Brewers within one victory of their first World Series appearance in 44 years.
Bauers turned an 11-pitch at-bat into a go-ahead two-run homer in the seventh inning as the Brewers took a commanding 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series with a 6-2 victory Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Milwaukee will aim for a sweep of the best-of-7 series tonight at Dodger Stadium.
Garrett Mitchell followed Bauers with a homer of his own as the Southern California natives put on a show in front of family and friends in a ballpark where the home team has played the bully for more than a decade.
“We play for each other. It’s as simple as that, man,” Bauers said. “Any time there’s a mistake, an error, a walk, pitchers give up runs, hitters strike out in a big spot, the only thing anybody’s thinking about is how can I help pick that guy up? How can I help pick that guy up and do my part to win this game?”
Rookie left-hander Robert Gasser gave up three hits over five scoreless innings as the Brewers moved closer to the franchise’s second trip to the World Series. The Brewers made their lone Fall Classic appearance in 1982 as an American League team, losing in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals.
Jackson Chourio led off the game with a first-pitch homer off Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell as Milwaukee showed its power capabilities after finishing last in the National League in homers during the regular season with 154.
“Job’s not finished yet,” Mitchell said. “Just got to take it a day at a time, not really worried about what’s happened today, what happened yesterday or what’s coming tomorrow. We’ve just got to show up and continue to play our brand of baseball and continue doing it for one another.”
Will Smith hit a two-run double for the Dodgers, who won the past two World Series titles. Los Angeles is trying to become the first National League club to win three consecutive Fall Classic championships.
Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts moved Shohei Ohtani to sixth in the batting order with the superstar in a postseason slump. Ohtani went 1-for-2 with a walk and a hit-by-pitch. The Dodgers’ offense was held to five hits in Game 3 after collecting three in Game 2.
“I haven’t digested this one,” Roberts said when asked about potential lineup changes for Game 4. “They’re going to run a bullpen game. Just trying to figure out which guys we want to be in there, how you kind of construct the lineup, but I haven’t thought about that one yet.”
Snell appeared to recover from Chourio’s ambush home run before he was rocked by consecutive home runs with no outs in the seventh. Snell (0-1) allowed four runs on four hits in six-plus innings with two walks and nine strikeouts.
“I just left the fastball over the middle to Bauers,” said Snell, who was in the Tampa Bay Rays organization with Bauers from 2015-18. “… I’ve seen the ups and downs he’s been through, and it’s been a lot of downs. So for him to go through this right now, he’s earned it. Hats off to him. What an at-bat.”
Trailing 1-0 from the jump, the Dodgers managed to put their leadoff batter on base in four of the first six innings before finally breaking through.
Gasser was replaced by right-hander Abner Uribe to open the sixth inning, and the reliever walked three of the first four batters he faced to load the bases, including a walk to Ohtani. Smith delivered a double off the wall in left-center field for a 2-1 lead after entering the game in a 1-for-25 slump.
Los Angeles failed to add onto the lead in the inning against left-hander DL Hall (3-0) when Enrique Hernandez and Tommy Edman struck out to end the threat.
Milwaukee responded immediately when Andrew Vaughn walked to open the seventh before Bauers’ epic at-bat. Two pitches later, Mitchell went over the wall in right-center field for a 4-2 advantage to end Snell’s outing.
Bauers had a similar plate appearance in Game 2 when he worked a 12-pitch walk with two outs in the third inning and Christian Yelich followed with a two-run single.
“Yeah, there was for sure a moment where I thought to myself like, ‘Oh, you’re in it again,’” Bauers said. “As far as the approach for the at-bat, I didn’t want to miss a fastball.”
The Brewers added to their lead in the eighth when Brice Turang scored on a Justin Wrobleski wild pitch, and Joey Ortiz tacked on an RBI single in the ninth.
Hall threw 2⅓ scoreless innings. Brewers closer Trevor Megill got the last four outs, striking out the final two batters, for his fourth save of the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
After setting a franchise record with an MLB-best 103 wins in the 2026 regular season, the Brewers are vying for their first World Series appearance since 1982, which remains the only trip to the fall classic in franchise history.
Chourio pounced on the first pitch of Game 3 of the National League Championship Series from Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, parking it over the right-center-field fence for a home run. It was his sixth career postseason dinger at just 22 years old, breaking a tie with Contreras -- who has three long balls in the 2026 playoffs -- for the most in Brewers postseason history.
With both in mind, who is each team’s all-time postseason home run king? Here’s a breakdown of the players who hold a franchise’s playoff home run record.
American League East
Blue Jays: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. -- 8
Vladdy put together one of the single greatest individual postseason performances we’ve ever seen in 2025, leading the Blue Jays all the way to Game 7 of the World Series. After starting his postseason career with six homer-less games, Guerrero hit all eight of his October long balls in ‘25. He surpassed José Bautista (six) for the most home runs in Blue Jays playoff history. The dinger that earned Guerrero the franchise lead came off of Shohei Ohtani in the World Series, no less.
Orioles: Frank Robinson -- 9
The Hall of Famer had a knack for the clutch. Robinson's 26 career walk-off hits (regular season and postseason) are the most by any player since RBI became official in 1920. That knack extended to the playoffs, where Robinson posted an .887 OPS and slammed 10 total homers, including a franchise-best nine with the Orioles. Robinson won World Series MVP in 1966 after hitting go-ahead home runs in Games 1 and 4 of a Baltimore sweep over the Dodgers.
Rays: Randy Arozarena -- 11
Arozarena put the Rays on his back in the 2020 postseason, recording 29 hits -- at the time the most in a single postseason. Ten of those hits were home runs, giving Arozarena another single-postseason record and pulling him ahead of Evan Longoria (nine) for the most playoff homers in Rays franchise history. Oh, and Arozarena did all of this as a rookie. He tagged one more postseason big fly with the Rays in '21 before joining the Mariners via trade in 2024.
Red Sox: David Ortiz -- 17
Big Papi was an October legend in the truest sense of the phrase. His walk-off heroics helped the Red Sox overcome a 3-0 series deficit in the 2004 ALCS, paving the way for a curse-breaking World Series title. Ortiz’s 17 playoff home runs included two walk-offs and six with the Red Sox facing elimination.
Yankees: Bernie Williams -- 22
Williams played in the postseason in 12 consecutive years from 1995-2006, with huge moments at several turns. His 1996 performance -- an 1.142 OPS with six homers -- is one of the best postseasons of all time. Overall, his 22 long balls are fifth most by any player in playoff history, sharing a list with other Yankees legends like Derek Jeter (20) and Mickey Mantle (18).
AL Central
Guardians: Jim Thome -- 17
Thome hit all 17 of his postseason homers with Cleveland. He’s one of three players with multiple postseason grand slams, along with Francisco Lindor and Jason Varitek. Thome's grand slams came in Game 6 of the 1998 ALCS against the Yankees and Game 2 of the 1999 ALDS against the Red Sox.
Royals: George Brett -- 10
Brett is one of just 12 players who have hit three home runs in a single postseason game. His herculean effort came in Game 3 of the 1978 ALCS against the Yankees. Even though in defeat, Brett memorably whacked three pitches over the fence, one out to left field, one over the center-field fence, and one to right field.
Tigers: Miguel Cabrera -- 9
Cabrera’s most memorable postseason may have come as a rookie with the championship-winning Marlins in 2003 (more on that soon). But his most impactful playoff performance happened in 2011, when he launched four home runs with a 1.261 OPS in 11 games for the Tigers. He later passed Delmon Young’s eight career playoff home runs as a Tiger with a solo shot in Game 1 of the 2014 ALDS.
Twins: Kirby Puckett -- 5
Goose Goslin is the Twins' franchise leader in postseason home runs with seven, but Puckett holds the record since the club moved to Minnesota in 1961. Puckett took two trips to the postseason with the Twins, winning the World Series both times (1987 and 1991). The Hall of Famer was particularly impactful in ‘91, when he hit four dingers on an overall .333/.396/.667 slash line. That included an iconic 11th-inning walk-off homer in Game 6 of the Fall Classic.
White Sox: Paul Konerko -- 7
Konerko mashed five of his seven postseason homers during Chicago's 2005 title run, narrowly besting teammate Paul Crede (four HR) for the franchise lead. Konerko hit two of his long balls while earning ALCS MVP honors, then later launched a go-ahead grand slam in Game 2 of the World Series to down the Astros.
AL West
Angels: Troy Glaus -- 9
Glaus hit seven of his nine postseason homers with the Angels during the club's World Series campaign in 2022. Three of those were go-ahead long balls in the sixth inning or later, which is tied with the Astros' Yordan Alvarez (2022) for the most such home runs in a single postseason.
Athletics: José Canseco -- 7
In addition to holding the club's all-time postseason home run record, Canseco holds a share of the record for the most homers in a single postseason by an A's player. He slugged four big flies in 1988, helping lead the Athletics to the AL Pennant. Two years later, Canseco passed Al Simmons for the most postseason home runs in A's franchise history with a dinger in Game 2 of the 1990 World Series.
Astros: Jose Altuve -- 28
Altuve added to his stature as one of baseball's best postseason hitters in 2026. He clubbed a solo shot in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series against the White Sox, putting him one home run behind Manny Ramirez for most all-time. And Altuve tends to meet the moment, too: A whopping 14 of his playoff homers have been of the game-tying or go-ahead variety, the most such homers in postseason history.
Mariners: Jay Buhner and Edgar Martinez -- 8
Buhner and Martinez each starred for the Mariners during the most successful era in franchise history, as the club made the playoffs four times between 1994 and 2001. Buhner took the early lead in career postseason homers, hitting four in ‘95 and two more in ‘97. But Martinez caught up to his longtime teammate in 2001 with a pair of long balls in the 2001 ALDS.
Rangers: Nelson Cruz -- 14
Cruz authored a historic postseason moment when he hit the first walk-off grand slam in postseason history in Game 2 of the 2011 ALCS against the Tigers. It remains one of just two walk-off postseason slams after Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman also accomplished the feat in Game 1 of the 2024 World Series. Cruz, the owner of 464 regular-season home runs, hit his last postseason homer at age 41 with the Rays, becoming the second-oldest player to go yard in a playoff game.
National League East
Braves: Chipper Jones -- 13
Jones starred for an Atlanta team that made 11 consecutive postseason appearances from 1995-2005. The eight-time All-Star broke onto the October stage in a big way in ‘95, slugging two home runs -- including the game-winning shot in the ninth inning -- in a 5-4 win over the Rockies in Game 1 of the NLDS. Jones and Austin Riley are the only two players in Braves history with multiple go-ahead homers in the eighth inning or later of a postseason game.
Marlins: Miguel Cabrera -- 4
A 20-year-old, baby-faced Cabrera looked at home in his first postseason in 2003, steering the Florida Marlins to the franchise’s second World Series title. Cabrera launched four home runs in the ‘03 playoffs -- his only with the Marlins -- which stands as the most home runs in a single postseason at age 20 or younger in MLB history. With a long ball off Yankees right-hander Roger Clemens in Game 4 of the World Series, Cabrera became the second youngest player to go yard in the Fall Classic.
Mets: Daniel Murphy -- 7
All seven of Murphy’s playoff home runs with the Mets came during a magical two-week stretch in 2015. The second baseman homered in six straight postseason games -- spanning Game 4 of the NLDS through Game 4 of the NLCS -- to steer the Mets to the NL Pennant. That’s the longest streak in a single postseason in MLB history. Even more impressive, Murphy homered off three former Cy Young winners: Clayton Kershaw, Zack Greinke and Jake Arrieta.
Nationals: Bryce Harper, Juan Soto, Anthony Rendon and Ryan Zimmerman -- 5
Four of the most iconic players in Nationals franchise history (since the team moved from Montreal to Washington) share this distinction. Youth is a popular theme here. At 19 years old and 362 days, Harper became the second-youngest player in MLB history to homer in a postseason game when he went deep in Game 5 of the 2012 NLDS. Seven years later, Soto (20 years, 346 days) became the sixth-youngest player to homer in the playoffs, teeing off for a two-run shot in Game 3 of the 2019 NLDS.
Phillies: Kyle Schwarber -- 13
Schwarber is one of the most prolific power hitters in playoff history: His 24 career playoff home runs rank third most all time, trailing only Ramirez and Altuve. He’s crushed 15 homers in a Phillies uniform, the latest being a 447-foot shot in Game 2 of the 2026 NL Wild Card Series against the Braves. In 2022, Schwarber keyed a stirring run to the World Series with three home runs in the NLCS against the Padres and three more dingers in the Fall Classic against the Astros.
NL Central
Brewers: Jackson Chourio -- 6
Chourio tattooed a pair of home runs to help the Brewers stave off elimination in Game 2 of the 2024 NL Wild Card Series, becoming the second-youngest player in postseason history with a multi-HR game (20 years & 205 days). He’s the only player in postseason history with a leadoff home run under age 22 -- which he’s done three times -- and the only player in MLB history with six playoff home runs before turning 23. Chourio's leadoff dinger off Blake Snell in Game 3 of the NLCS against the Dodgers as his latest feat of strength.
Cardinals: Albert Pujols -- 13
Who else but The Machine? Pujols slugged 19 career playoff home runs -- T-7th most all time -- including 13 with the Cardinals. The future Hall of Famer tagged Randy Johnson for his first career playoff homer in Game 2 of the 2001 NLDS, a surefire sign of things to come. Pujols is one of just 12 players to go deep three times in a postseason game, doing so in Game 3 of the 2011 World Series. He also launched one of the most iconic home runs in franchise history with a go-ahead, three-run shot onto the train tracks in Houston off All-Star closer Brad Lidge in Game 5 of the 2005 NLCS.
Cubs: Kris Bryant, Anthony Rizzo and Kyle Schwarber -- 6
Talk about a fitting trio: These three All-Stars propelled the Cubs to a curse-breaking, legacy-defining World Series title in 2016. Bryant (2) and Rizzo (1) each launched home runs in the Fall Classic, keying victories in Games 5 and 6 to spur a historic 3-1 series comeback. Schwarber, one of the best postseason power hitters of all time, launched six of his 24 playoff homers with the Cubs, including five dingers in his introduction to playoff baseball in 2015.
Pirates: Willie Stargell -- 7
The Hall of Fame slugger managed just two home runs while hitting .217 across his first 26 postseason games, spanning five different playoff appearances. But Stargell flipped the script in his age-39 season in 1979, smashing five home runs while earning NLCS and World Series MVP honors. Stargell’s two-run blast in the sixth inning of Game 7 of the ‘79 World Series proved to be the World Series-winning hit.
Reds: Johnny Bench -- 10
Bench played in 10 postseason series across his illustrious 17-year career and, rather remarkably, homered in all but one of them -- only going without a long ball in the 1975 NLCS. The Hall of Fame catcher’s only multi-HR playoff series came in the 1976 Fall Classic, when he swatted a pair of homers, posted a 1.667 OPS and took home World Series MVP honors for the Big Red Machine.
NL West
D-backs: Chris Young -- 5
Young only played in 12 postseason games for Arizona, but that was plenty of time to rewrite the franchise record books. His leadoff home run in Game 3 of the 2007 NLDS against the Cubs’ Rich Hill accounts for the only leadoff home run in D-backs franchise history. Four years later, Young slammed a pair of long balls in Game 4 of the NLDS against the Brewers. It remains the only multi-HR game by a Diamondbacks’ hitter in franchise history.
Dodgers: Max Muncy -- 19
Muncy homered three times in the 2026 NLDS against the Braves, pushing his total to 19 playoff home runs and extending the most in Dodgers postseason history. It’s a remarkable record for Muncy to hold, given his journey: He first joined the Dodgers organization on a Minor League contract in 2017, after he was released by the Athletics. The three-time All-Star owns some of the most important home runs in Dodgers history. That includes his 18th-inning walk-off in Game 3 of the 2018 World Series and his eighth-inning home run in Game 7 of the 2025 Fall Classic, which set the stage for a stirring late-game comeback.
Giants: Barry Bonds -- 8
Bonds made the postseason only four times in 15 seasons with the Giants. And while he launched more home runs (756) than anyone in baseball history, Bonds actually was held without a home run in three of those four trips to October. All eight of his playoff home runs with San Francisco came in 2002, when he posted a 1.559 OPS in 17 games while leading the Giants to the NL Pennant. The most memorable occurred in the ninth inning of Game 2 of the World Series, when he clobbered a blast to right field off closer Troy Percival. Arozarena (10, 2020 Rays) is the only player with more home runs in a single postseason.
Padres: Manny Machado -- 9
Machado extended his own franchise record in his first at-bat of the 2026 postseason, launching a home run in the first inning of Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against the Cubs’ Matthew Boyd. Machado ushered in a new era of baseball in San Diego when he signed a 10-year deal ahead of the 2019 season, and the Padres have made the playoffs in five of the eight years since. The seven-time All-Star was at his best in the 2022 playoffs, helping San Diego win a pair of postseason series thanks to four home runs in 12 games.
Rockies: Matt Holliday -- 5
Holliday is responsible for one of the defining moments in Rockies history, although it has nothing to do with a home run: He belly-flopped into home plate to score the game-winning run in Game 163 in 2007, giving Colorado the Wild Card tiebreaker over San Diego. That mad dash set the stage for Holliday's only postseason stint with the club, which was wildly successful. The seven-time All-Star homered in each of his first two playoff games in the NLDS against the Phillies, and wound up with five long balls as the Rockies earned the franchise’s first World Series berth.

As summer comes to a close and the air turns crisp, you know what's coming: the MLB Playoffs. The NFL season is already underway, and if you're also a baseball lover, this next month is essential viewing. The MLB has been through a number of changes in recent years. From the universal DH and the pitch clock to video replay and an automated strike zone, baseball may look very different if you haven't been paying attention.
This week, the Dodgers will go head-to-head against the Brewers, and the Guardians will face the Rays in the best-of-seven Championship series. Which teams will come out on top? Here's how you can watch live.
What Time Is the Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians Game?
Today's game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers will take place on Tuesday, October 13 at 8 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians?
American League Division Series games will be broadcast on TBS, while National League games will be on Fox and FS1. You can also watch them with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fox One, Fubo, HBO Max, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Rays vs. the Guardians for Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to this weekend's games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB Playoffs Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. Things started off with the best-of-three Wild Card Series, where the Braves, Padres, White Sox, and Yankees advanced. The best-of-five Division Series put them up against the Los Angeles Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers, Cleveland Guardians, and Tampa Bay Rays, respectively. All of whom managed to advance
Now, the Rays and Guardians and Dodgers and Brewers meet in the best-of-seven Championship Series to determine the best team in each league. The winner from each league will then advance to a best-of-seven World Series to begin on October 23. Who will make it all the way?
Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers - MIL lead 2-0
- Game 3 on October 14 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1
- Game 4 on October 15 @ 9 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1
- Game 5 on October 16 @ 9 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
- Game 6 on October 18 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
- Game 7 on October 19 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
Cleveland Guardians vs. Tampa Bay Rays - CLE leads 1-0
- Game 2 on October 13 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 3 on October 15 @ 6 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 16 @ 6 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max

- Game 6 on October 19 @ 5 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
- Game 7 on October 20 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
*if necessary
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. Additional rounds will be on other networks. ALDS and ALCS games are on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games are on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

Drew Rasmussen will face a familiar opponent when the Tampa Bay Rays open the American League Championship Series against the Cleveland Guardians on Monday. The right-hander is preparing to pitch against Steven Kwan, his former college teammate and longtime friend at Oregon State.
Rasmussen spoke warmly about Kwan ahead of the matchup, praising the Guardians outfielder's character as well as his ability. The two played together in college before establishing themselves in the major leagues.
"There's not enough great things I could say about the kid. He's perfect. He's unbelievable. He's one of the greatest human beings in the entire sport," Rasmussen said, according to ESPN reporter Buster Olney.
Drew Rasmussen is fired up to face his college teammate and longtime friend Steven Kwan in the playoffs: “There’s not enough great things I could say about the kid. He’s perfect. He’s unbelievable. He’s one of the greatest human beings in the entire sport.”
When Rasmussen faces…
— Buster Olney (@Buster_ESPN) October 11, 2026
Rasmussen also described the familiar exchange between the two when they meet on the field. "I definitely acknowledge every single time," he said. "Usually a little smile gets shot back in my direction. I mean, shoot, I was 19 the first time I faced him in fall ball at Oregon State."
The matchup carries added significance because Rasmussen enters the series after a dominant postseason start. He held the New York Yankees to one hit over eight scoreless innings in Game 1 of the American League Division Series, striking out 10 and allowing two walks as Tampa Bay won 1-0.
Rasmussen also delivered a strong regular season, finishing 2026 with a 16-5 record, a 2.67 ERA and 174 strikeouts across 172 innings. His performance gives Tampa Bay an experienced starter to lead its rotation into the matchup with Cleveland.
Kwan finished the regular season with a .282 batting average, a .382 on-base percentage, 152 hits and 10 stolen bases. The left fielder also helped Cleveland reach the ALCS after the Guardians defeated the Chicago White Sox in five games in the Division Series.
The Rays finished 98-64 and swept the Yankees in their ALDS, while Cleveland advanced after rallying from a two-game deficit against Chicago. The teams begin their best-of-seven series Monday at Tropicana Field, with Rasmussen scheduled to start for Tampa Bay.
The friendship between Rasmussen and Kwan will add a personal element to the opening game, but both players will have a clear job to do. Rasmussen will try to keep Cleveland's lineup in check, while Kwan will look to help the Guardians take an early lead in the series.

Baseball postseason, for all of its unpredictability, has brought us the meeting of the two best teams in the sport to determine the National League representative in the World Series. Ahead of last season's NLCS, the angle of David versus Goliath was heavily played in virtually any analysis—it didn't help the more centered angle that the Dodgers steamrolled the Brewers on their way to a sweep. This time around it might not be that simple.
The similarities are evident, with the Brewers, yet again, having home-field advantage as a team that better maximized its skill set in the regular season, all while the Dodgers remain the favorites to advance, as was the case last season. Having said that, foolish are those who project a similar imbalance to that of the previous NLCS—the expectation of a more tightly contested series goes through pitching.
It may appear like a small factor, but the fact that both teams won their Division Series in four games means that Pat Murphy and Dave Roberts can line up their pitching in the ideal way for this Championship Series. And pitching is the great equalizer here, as both teams are stacked in that department and neither offense is currently hot enough to the point of putting into question the likelihood of a series dominated by elite pitching.
For all the talent on the mound for the Dodgers, the odds-on favorite to win the NL Cy Young pitches on the other side in Jacob Misiorowski. He is joined by the rookie Logan Henderson at the front end of a pitching staff tied with the Dodgers for the second-highest ERA+ in baseball. Last year's Brewers ace, Freddy Peralta, was good, not great, in the series against Los Angeles, and that applied to several key Brewers pitchers in order for the Dodgers to sweep the series in four without major offensive explosions.
With starting pitching on both sides able to dominate, the Dodgers have an advantage from last season's team in that the bullpen brings a much greater sense of reliability, not only in depth but also in the backend. We probably get the sense most fans will watch Edwin Díaz and Tanner Scott, waiting for them to fail all the way until the hypothetical final out of the World Series—but they've done enough to earn Dave Roberts' trust, and the plethora of options behind them ready for a high-leverage spot if things go south isn't to be ignored.
Such emphasis on pitching is a must from the Brewers side because offensively, despite Jake Bauers' breakout campaign at first, the Dodgers still retain a heavy advantage, one that might even be currently underplayed ahead of the series. With little to no action from some of its top hitters, the Dodgers weren't brilliant, but they still got theirs in key spots against the feisty Braves. Last postseason, the Dodgers offense wasn't bombastic against Milwaukee, but it did enough to capitalize on strong pitching, while the Brewers' attack was nowhere to be found against elite Dodger starting pitching.
Second to last in regular-season homers and top five in stolen bases, the Brewers' offense's best course of action to put a dent in Dodger pitching is through generating action on the basepaths — putting the bat on the ball and pressuring a defense that has vulnerabilities (I won't name any names — Teoscar Hernández, cough, cough). It's nearly unfathomable to imagine Blake Snell or Tyler Glasnow escaping a five-walk outing with just one run against the Brewers like they did facing the Braves.
All season long, the National League has clearly proven to be the superior league. It's only fitting that the winner of the NLCS, whoever that is, will enter the Fall Classic as the favorite to win it all — the Dodgers in pursuit of a threepeat and the Brewers in search of their first title.

item.content:encoded:
To the victors go the spoils and the Tampa Bay Rays have earned every right to crow.
The plucky upstarts, who happened to win the American League East with the junior circuit's best record this year, completed a three-game sweep over the mighty New York Yankees on Wednesday night to secure a spot in the ALCS.
MORE: Jazz Chisholm 'confused' by Yankees' fans reaction
Everything this team does well was on full display as unheralded players continuously rose to the occasion. Junior Caminero, the Rays' sole superstar, went 3-for-10 in the series and worked two walks. Though he did not contribute much in the realm of power, the third baseman had plenty of energy to take up the mantle as chief trash-talker after the final out was recorded.
Caminero threw out a bit of everything in his defiant celebration. First there was the exaggerated sweeping motion to let a dejected Yankees Stadium crowd know just how thoroughly their beloved team had been beaten.
He continued the revelry by channeling David Ortiz and bellowing about the Yankees' loss.
Once in the clubhouse, his fire only burned brighter and by the time those suds-soaked interviews began, he was under the impression he was the best in the world.
There are a lot of not very fun people out there who shame baseball teams for celebrating like they've just won the World Series on every step to winning the World Series. By the time the Fall Classic wraps a squad can have four or five of these out-of-control parties under their belt.
And to be clear, most of them don't age well because only one franchise can win the whole dang thing.
But here's a rebuttal. Baseball is an insane marathon and there are thousands upon thousands of boring hours against the actual game action. Teams are together for seven or eight months and need every excuse they can to blow off some steam and celebrate what they've accomplished together.
Just think of how much Yankees fans are going to hate Caminero for his entire career now based on just a few clips. That is, if they don't use their considerable funds to take him away from small-market Tampa in a couple years. None of that would be possible without carte blanche to party it up and take every available opportunity to twist the knife.

As summer comes to a close and the air turns crisp, you know what's coming: the MLB Playoffs. The NFL season is already underway, and if you're also a baseball lover, this next month is essential viewing. The MLB has been through a number of changes in recent years. From the universal DH and the pitch clock to video replay and an automated strike zone, baseball may look very different if you haven't been paying attention.
This week, all Division Series matchups continue with the White Sox vs. Guardians, Braves vs. Dodgers, Yankees vs. Rays, and Padres vs. Brewers. American League games continue tonight, while National League matchups will pick up tomorrow. Don't want to miss a minute of the action? Here's how you can watch live.
What Time Is the White Sox vs. Guardians Game 2?
Today's game between the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians will take place on Monday, October 5 at 5 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Yankees vs. Rays Game 2?
Today's game between the New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays will take place on Monday, October 5 at 8:00 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Braves vs. Dodgers Game 3?
Tomorrow's game between the Atlanta Braves and Los Angeles Dodgers will take place on Tuesday, October 6 at 6 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Padres vs. Brewers Game 3?
Tomorrow's game between the San Diego Padres and Milwaukee Brewers will take place on Tuesday, October 6 at 9:30 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the MLB Division Series Games
American League Division Series games will be broadcast on TBS, while National League games will be on Fox and FS1. You can also watch them with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fox One, Fubo, HBO Max, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Games For Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to this weekend's games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB Playoffs Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. Things started off with the best-of-three Wild Card Series, where the Braves, Padres, White Sox, and Yankees advanced. Now, the best-of-five Division Series starts October 3. The Cleveland Guardians, Tampa Bay Rays, Los Angeles Dodgers, and Milwaukee Brewers will meet them.
After this round, the Championship Series extends to seven games to determine the best team in each league, who then advance to a best-of-seven World Series. Who will make it all the way?
Chicago White Sox vs. Cleveland Guardians - CWS lead 1-0:
- Game 2 on October 5 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 3 on October 7 @ 4:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 8 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 5 on October 10 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max

- Game 4 on October 7 @ 6:00 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 5 on October 9 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - Fox/Fox One

- Game 5 on October 10 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max

- Game 3 on October 6 @ 9:30 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 4 on October 7 @ 10:00 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 5 on October 9 @ 4:30 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. Additional rounds will be on other networks. ALDS and ALCS games are on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games are on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

After a disappointing end to the 2026 season, a prominent MLB insider believes the Philadelphia Phillies will consider trading long-time star Bryce Harper this winter.
The Phillies entered this year with the fourth-highest payroll in MLB and big expectations. While they didn’t win the National League East, the hope was that their talent-rich roster could still go on a deep run in the postseason. Unfortunately, despite their best efforts, Philadelphia came up short in their three-game Wild Card series against division rivals the Atlanta Braves.
Following their season-ending loss on Thursday, The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal claimed, “The Phillies at least need to kick around the idea of trading” the All-Star first baseman. A player the MLB insider feels doesn’t have an “oppressive” contract, with five years and $118 million left on the deal.
If the team pulled the trigger on a trade for the two-time NL MVP this winter, here are five teams he could end up landing with this winter.
Chicago Cubs
The Chicago Cubs had an equally frustrating finish to their 2026 campaign this week as well. However, they didn’t even get to three games, and the team with the sixth highest payroll in baseball was soundly beaten by the San Diego Padres in just two.
Chicago could lose both of their corner outfielders this winter, so Harper could fill either of those spots. Or the nine-time All-Star could be an option at DH. Either way, Harper would be a really nice addition to the lineup. Plus, like Alex Bregman, he is a strong veteran leader and player in the postseason.
Boston Red Sox
The Boston Red Sox are another team that saw their playoff run ended in just two games. In their case, it was rivals the New York Yankees who eliminated them. Harper could certainly be an option for Boston at DH. But the thing this team lacks the most, which he would address, is a proven veteran leader on the field and in the clubhouse. If he can handle the pressure of Philadelphia, Harper would be fine in Boston.
Toronto Blue Jays
This season was a massive disappointment for the Toronto Blue Jays. After being a couple of outs away from winning the World Series last fall, the Jays finished dead last in the AL East with a 79-83 record this year. So you can bet they will look to make a big move this offseason to get back into title contention in 2027.
If the Phillies actually make Harper available in trade talks, Toronto will be fascinated by the idea of pairing him with Vladimir Guerrero Jr. next season. If Guerrero Jr. can return to the player he always has been in 2027, and Kazuma Okamoto puts up similar power numbers, adding Harper to the batting order gives Toronto a spot in the order you can’t pitch around.
New York Yankees
The Yankees are still in the race to be champions in 2026. However, if they fall short of that yearly goal, the Yanks will surely look into adding a piece or two that can get them to end their 17-year title drought.
New York would need to find a new home for Giancarlo Stanton, but with only one guaranteed season for $15 million left on his deal, it may be possible this offseason. If they can trade the injury-prone five-time All-Star, a lineup with a healthy Aaron Judge, Harper, Ben Rice, and Cody Bellinger is one of the best in baseball.
St. Louis Cardinals
While the St. Louis Cardinals finished 77-85 this season, they seemed a bit ahead of schedule in their rebuild because of the upside in young stars JJ Wetherholt and Jordan Walker. The Cards are willing to make bold moves for proven stars if they feel they can help get the team to the next level or change the culture for the better. Harper could do both.
With St. Louis having a top-five farm system in MLB, they would certainly have the prospect assets to easily get a deal done.

LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers set their trade deadline sights on one big target and landed him in Tarik Skubal. The two-time Cy Young Award winner will get the call to start Game 1 of the National League Division Series on Saturday at Dodger Stadium against the Atlanta Braves.
Fabian Ardaya at The Athletic was first to report Skubal getting the call in Game 1.
Skubal started two Games 1 with the Detroit Tigers, and in six postseason starts over 2024-25 has a 2.04 ERA with 56 strikeouts against five unintentional walks in 39 2/3 innings, and has lasted at least six innings in all six starts.
When the Dodgers acquired Skubal from the Tigers on August 2, president of baseball operations noted the team's singular focus at this year's trade deadline.
"We were of the mind to be aggressive for one player, and fortunately we were able to line up," Friedman said at the time. "As we've talked about a lot, whenever there's a star-level player available who can really shift championship odds, those are the moments we'll be more aggressive."
Yoshinobu Yamamoto started Game 1 of the 2024 NLDS, and is coming off one of the best postseasons in MLB history, 5-1 with a 1.45 ERA in 37 1/3 innings. That included consecutive complete games in the NLCS and World Series, and he won all three of his appearances in the Fall Classic, including getting the final eight outs of Game 7 one day after starting and pitching six innings to win Game 6.
Blake Snell has five career starts in Game 1, including twice for the Dodgers last year in the wild card round and NLCS. Tyler Glasnow, with four career Game 1 starts, rounds out the rotation.
"To be honest, we can kind of really put all four guys in a hat, and run them out there," manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday.
"Our pitching staff is pretty special, in my opinion," first baseman Freddie Freeman said. "We got four number ones rolling out there, with Yama, Snell, Skubs, and Glasnow."
Skubal has been just about everything the Dodgers could have wanted when they traded for the two-time Cy Young Award winner on August 2. In 10 starts with Los Angeles, the left-hander had a 2.61 ERA and 2.84 xERA with 70 strikeouts and 13 walks in 62 innings.

To begin their quest for a third-straight World Series this postseason, the Dodgers will turn to the one pitcher in their rotation yet to win a championship ring.
Tarik Skubal is expected to be named the team’s starter for Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves on Saturday, a source with knowledge of the situation told the California Post, giving the reigning two-time Cy Young Award winner and marquee trade deadline acquisition an immediate opportunity to jump-start the club’s three-peat bid.
The Dodgers, of course, had no bad options for their playoff opener.
Their rotation includes four pitchers who would be No. 1 options on most other clubs, with Skubal being joined by Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow for this year’s October push.
However, Skubal is set to get the nod, as The Athletic first reported, after increasingly impressive late-season performances with the Dodgers following his blockbuster arrival from the Detroit Tigers in August.
The 29-year-old left-hander posted a 5-2 record and 2.61 ERA in 10 post-deadline starts with the club, improving upon the 7-5 mark and 2.79 ERA he had with the Tigers during a first half that was sidetracked by an elbow procedure that sidelined him for all of May.
Skubal’s best outings came in the final weeks of the regular season, when he spun a pair of scoreless seven-inning starts in two of his final three appearances of the campaign.
Prior to Friday’s news, there was a thought that Yamamoto would be the Dodgers’ Game 1 starter, given his World Series MVP heroics last fall.
But Yamamoto threw extensively in a simulated game on Wednesday, during the club’s bye week workouts. That kept him on his customary once-per-week pitching schedule (his regular-season finale came on the Wednesday before that) and might line him up to pitch in Game 3 in Atlanta next Tuesday instead. Of note: Yamamoto has notably better splits on the road (1.77 ERA) than at home (3.13 ERA) this year.
Snell, who has followed Skubal in the Dodgers’ rotation lately, seems like the logical candidate to start Game 2 on Sunday. Glasnow, who pitched in another simulated game Thursday, figures to go in Game 4, and could be an option out of the bullpen this weekend.
While Skubal –– who will be the sport’s top free agent this winter –– has yet to win a World Series, he does have a sterling postseason track record.
In six playoff outings over the last two years with the Tigers, he pitched to a 2.04 ERA while striking out 56 batters in 39 ⅔ innings. Those numbers would be even better if not for his one October clunker, when he gave up five runs in a winner-take-all loss in Game 5 of the 2024 American League Division Series.
That failure has become a motivator for Skubal in the two years since. It has left him with a feeling of unfinished business as he begins another playoff campaign amid new surroundings now.
“Once the months change and the playoffs start, nothing matters,” he said last week. “It’s just about winning that game, and that’s how I treat every single start. Because I’m just trying to put our team in a position to win a baseball game. That won’t change from today, and whenever my next start is.”

item.content:encoded:
The Diamondbacks' end-of-year press conferences on Thursday, Oct. 1, largely were dominated by talk of manager Torey Lovullo's return for another year. Coming off another playoff miss, it seemed possible Lovullo might be out. Instead, he received a two-year deal.
But there were a few more nuggets that came from general manager Mike Hazen's portion of the afternoon. Here is a look at a few other topics that were explored during his 20-plus minute session with reporters.
Will Ketel Marte be back for another season?
Hazen sidestepped any questions about Marte's future, saying he had yet to take a look at roster construction for next season. But he did seem to acknowledge the argument for moving on from him after another season in which Marte created drama for an unexcused absence.
"I think you win with star players in this game," Hazen said. "But I am also — I've said this — I'm not blind to what the clubhouse dynamic is and what the interaction between all the players and the coaches and how that comes into winning and losing games."
Moreover, in the days surrounding Marte's return from the restricted and injured lists in late August/early September, players seemed to intimate that they expected Marte to be moved over the winter. Multiple players made comments about getting through the year and "dealing with the situation" after the season.
Where does the blame fall for 2026?
As is often the case, Hazen largely took responsibility for the team falling two games short of a playoff appearance with an 86-76 record. He made multiple references to not doing enough in the offseason to add to the first base and designated hitter positions and to the moves he was unable to make at the trade deadline, including upgrading those positions and adding a starting pitcher.
"Clearly didn't do enough," he said. "Left the team naked in places that it didn't need to be left naked, and we fell short by a game or two. I could go back and look at a million different ways where one or two things lead to one or two more wins, but that's one of them, too."
He also noted the fact that his team has had some tough luck in recent playoff misses. In 2024, they won 89 games but missed out via tiebreakers against the New York Mets and Atlanta Braves. And then this year they won more than three of the six teams that reached the postseason in the American League.
"It's hard for me to criticize 89 wins as, like, a failed season, even though you don't make the playoffs," he said. "It's hard for me to have more wins than half the American League playoff teams and just say that we were a failure when we all play the same schedule. But there's no excuse. We didn't make it."
What roster moves will they look to make this offseason?
The first area Hazen noted was a fairly obvious one: the need to improve against right-handed pitching, namely in the aforementioned first base/DH roles. Both were obvious areas of weakness this season.
Against right-handed pitching, the Diamondbacks hit .235/.309/.388 for a .697 OPS that ranked 26th in the majors. They had the lowest OPS at first base (.636) and the third-lowest at DH (.630) in the majors.
"The offseason priorities, from an add standpoint, are certainly going to be somewhere being a little more left-handed," Hazen said. "We struggled versus right-handed pitching this year. So that's a clear and obvious one."
Hazen also made a reference to wanting to "continue to improve our defense," though he acknowledged that might be a more "subtle" upgrade, perhaps suggesting he wants stronger bench/depth options than what the Diamondbacks had this year.

MLB playoff predictions 2026: Expert picks for every ALDS, NLDS series originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
October has officially arrived, just in time for the MLB postseason to ramp up.
With all four Wild Card series now over — three of which ended in two-game sweeps — just eight teams remain alive in the pursuit of a World Series title, with the Guardians, Rays, Dodgers and Brewers entering the picture after watching the first round from home.
Some of baseball's biggest stars, from Shohei Ohtani and Jacob Misiorowski to Junior Caminero and Cam Schlittler, will be on full display for the division series. On both sides of the bracket, the question will be whether the teams carrying their Wild Card momentum can now take down a well-rested heavyweight.
With a chance to reset between rounds, the best-of-five ALDS and NLDS matchups begin Saturday. Who will advance to the championship series?
With Wild Card matchups in the rearview mirror, The Sporting News predicts the 2026 MLB division series matchups.
MORE: Complete MLB playoff schedule for 2026 postseason
No. 6 Chicago White Sox vs. No. 2 Cleveland Guardians
You can certainly debate whether the Guardians (85 regular-season wins) or White Sox (84 regular-season wins) really belong on the postseason stage this season, with neither AL Central squad owning a ton of big-name star power. Regardless, the fact is that Cleveland and Chicago both find themselves with an opportunity to make a serious postseason run in a weaker AL bracket — and the White Sox have already taken advantage.
Chicago enters the ALDS the momentum of its first postseason series win since the 2005 World Series, proving in the Wild Card round that it has the power and pitching depth to challenge opponents. Cleveland, though, has better top-end starting pitching in Parker Messick, Gavin Williams and Tanner Bibee.
These two teams are well familiar with each other; the White Sox won the season series, 7-6. Cleveland's offense isn't very threatening, ranking last among all postseason teams in team OPS (.696) — this matchup will likely come down to how early the White Sox's bats can get to Guardians starters.
Saturday will mark the first time in MLB history that the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland have met in the postseason.
The White Sox began playing baseball in 1894 as the Sioux City Cornhuskers.
The Guardians began playing baseball in 1896 as the Columbus Buckeyes/Senators.
The fact that this is a divisional matchup means it will likely be close, but Chicago's momentum is hard to ignore, and there was only a one-win discrepancy between the sides in the regular season. The White Sox are finally building something serious, seemingly with a new hero every night. The power in Will Venable's lineup is dangerous enough to reach the ALCS.
Prediction: White Sox in 4
No. 4 New York Yankees vs. No. 1 Tampa Bay Rays
It's been clear since the start of the postseason that whichever AL East team emerged from the lower half of the bracket would be favored to reach the World Series. This is the heavyweight matchup of the two ALDS series, featuring elite starting pitching on both sides and some of MLB's premiere sluggers.
Of course, the massive question lingering over this matchup is how much, if at all, Aaron Judge will play for the Yankees. Even as the lower seed, if he's near 100 percent, it's hard not to view New York as the favorite to reach the ALCS; a healthy Judge, alongside Cody Bellinger, Luis Garcia Jr. and Ben Rice, takes Aaron Boone's lineup to a new level, capable of matching the all-around offensive excellence of Tampa Bay's quartet: Caminero, Yandy Siaz, Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson.
The Rays won this season series 7-6, but it may be the most evenly matched division series. Both sides can roll out a trio talented starters — New York with Cam Schlittler, Max Fried and Gerrit Cole, and Tampa Bay with Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez and Shane McClanahan — to pair with deep offenses.
Yankees can line up their pitching as follows against the Rays:
Game 1: Gerrit Cole
Game 2: Cam Schlittler
Game 3: Max Fried
Game 4: Gerrit Cole
Game 5: Cam Schlittler
For two reasons, the Yankees are the pick here. For one, between Schlittler and arguably the best bullpen in baseball, New York is loaded with leverage arms. And the Yankees are also riding high off a dominant Wild Card series, biding time for Judge and Giancarlo Stanton to heal. Assuming those two sluggers can at least be used in some key at-bats, the Yankees' lineup is capable of changing games in an instant.
Prediction: Yankees in 5
No. 3 Atlanta Braves vs. No. 2 Los Angeles Dodgers
The Dodgers' path to becoming the first National League team to win three-straight World Series will begin with a matchup against a 94-win Braves squad fresh off a Wild Card win over the Phillies.
Los Angeles' rest advantage could be significant. Even if he's not pitching, Ohtani has been dealing with lingering injury concerns over the last few months. A week off between his last regular season game should only benefit him, not to mention the Dodgers' ability to line up their loaded starting rotation however they choose. With the Braves using Chris Sale in two games against Philadelphia, he may not be available early in the NLDS.
The Dodgers and Braves have built quite the postseason history. 👀🔥
2013 NLDS — LAD def. ATL
2018 NLDS — LAD def. ATL
2020 NLCS — LAD def. ATL
2021 NLCS — ATL def. LAD
2026 NLDS — ??? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/mHhbDO9gDX
The top of Atlanta's lineup is potent enough to make this an interesting series, and the team did beat the Dodgers five times in the regular season, but Ronald Acuna Jr., Austin Riley and Ozzie Albies will have to meet the moment in the NLDS. Yoshinobu Yamamoto has pitched well against Atlanta in his career, as have Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow.
Even if the Braves' bats can keep things close, it's hard to imagine Atlanta's pitching staff beyond Sale being able to contain Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts over a five-game series. The Braves are a good team, but the Dodgers are far too talented to fall this early in the bracket.
Prediction: Dodgers in 4
No. 4 San Diego Padres vs. No. 1 Milwaukee Brewers
This matchup pins baseball's best team all season, Milwaukee, against one of its hottest over the past month, San Diego. While the Brewers are the clear favorites here, between the best starting pitcher in the game this season and a deep lineup that plays to contact, the Padres do pose some interesting challenges, going 4-2 against Milwaukee in the regular season.
On one hand, San Diego has stars made for October. As shown in the Wild Card round, when the top of the Padres' lineup is on, they're a hard team to beat — Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado, Xander Boegarts, Ty France and Jackson Merrill can look like one of the best 1-through-5 groups in baseball at times. Add in an elite starter (Michael King) and a strong bullpen led by Mason Miller, and there's a path for the Padres to pull off a stunner here.
Most data has shown that the more of a threat a team is to hit the ball out of the yard, the better they'll fare in the postseason. If this is finally going to be the year the Brewers reach a World Series — putting an end to their cycle of regular season success with playoff shortcomings — they'll need to slug more. This is an offense that's outstanding at making contact and getting on base, but has also continually come up short in October and finished second-to-last in team home runs (154) in the 2026 regular season.
Chances are, Milwaukee won't only be able to rely on its strong pitching staff to reach the World Series. The Brewers' bats will need some extra-base hits. But with the Padres' lackluster starting pitching depth, this is still a series the Brewers can claim even if they're not pristine.
San Diego may have some top-end talent and momentum, but the Padres can't match Milwaukee's all-around depth.
Prediction: Brewers in 4

If only this month, root for the small-market Rays and Brewers. A World Series appearance by either or both might weaken the owners’ argument for a salary cap just enough to save next season. It wouldn’t hurt baseball, either, for Brewers long-limbed right-hander Jacob Misiorowski, he of the 100-plus mph delivery, the most strikeouts and a 1.80 ERA, to be featured on the biggest stage.
An extinct breed: If you’re wondering how many 20-game winners MLB has had this season, stop looking. There are none. Such is the state of the game.
Done and dusted: Just like that, the Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong, the presumptive NL MVP with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases, is out of the playoffs after going hitless in two games against the Padres. That’s baseball.
Early services: Sunday’s Commanders-Colts from London is one of six 9:30 a.m. NFL starts from across the Atlantic in the next seven weeks. Far too many. It still is American football, isn’t it?
Disrespect: The Packers have been so listless this season that Fox moved their Nov. 11 game against the Bears from a late afternoon national window to 1 p.m. That’s a very early flex, but still leaves six nationally televised standalone Green Bay games on the schedule. Though not, the way things are going, for long.
No guarantees: The Rams, who some media magpies said could go undefeated, have already dropped two games in addition to losing quarterback sacker Myles Garrett for six weeks due to injury. The NFL is a cruel mistress.
An odd pairing: Nobody should ever underestimate the now 3-0 Chiefs. But a month ago, who could have imagined that the only Week 4 NFL game between unbeatens would include the Raiders?
In passing: This is my annual reminder that the Colts’ helmet is the best-looking helmet in football.
A team effort: Brian Schottenheimer apologized for mismanaging the end of the game against the Ravens, but the systemic blame for the Cowboys’ loss falls on Jerry Jones, who hired an inexperienced, first-time head coach who won’t cast much of a shadow over Jerry’s ego.
Idle thought: The most dangerous place to stand is between Jones and a TV camera.
Par for the course: The only thing the just completed Presidents Cup had in common with the last Ryder Cup were the scattered boorish shouts and chants from the American gallery.
For what it’s worth: It’s premature to assume the Protect College Sports Act will pass the House of Representatives. Or to think that the bill won’t introduce a new set of challenges and problems.
Roundball: NBA camps are open, and while most of the attention is on LeBron joining Philly, don’t sleep on the Heat now that Giannis Antetokounmpo has taken his talents to South Beach.
Great handle: A spectacular game against Alabama on Saturday would further boost the Heisman hopes of Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor, but the MSU player that catches my eye is running back Fluff Bothwell. He’s a cinch to make the All-Name Team.

For the 14th straight year, the Dodgers are postseason-bound.
Winners of three of the past six World Series, the Dodgers are looking to continue their reign. The back-to-back defending champions are bidding for the Major Leagues' first three-peat since the Yankees won three straight titles from 1998-2000.
The Dodgers, the No. 2 seed in the National League, are just about at full strength now that the likes of Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki have returned from the injured list, but there are several other compelling storylines to follow before the postseason.
Here's what to watch as the NL West-champion Dodgers forge their path back to the Fall Classic:
What could the postseason roster look like?
The strength of the Dodgers' pitching staff is the rotation, so expect them to carry more starters than they need and get creative with using some of them in relief. Manager Dave Roberts indicated that the team may carry only 12 pitchers to make room for an additional position player on the bench in the NL Division Series.
It may be premature to pencil in Josue De Paula, as the organization’s top prospect has played in only 11 big league games. But the Dodgers liked what they saw, and he could be an impact lefty bat off the bench.

First baseman (1): Freddie Freeman
Second baseman (1): Tommy Edman
Shortstop (1): Mookie Betts
Third baseman (1): Max Muncy

Utility/bench (3): Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim
Two-way player (1): Shohei Ohtani

When does the postseason begin?
The NL Division Series begin on Saturday.
Who could be the Dodgers' NLDS opponent? 
The Dodgers won their 13th NL West title in the past 14 seasons and secured a first-round bye, so they will play the winner of the Wild Card Series between the Braves and the Phillies.
Against which teams do the Dodgers have home-field advantage?
The Dodgers have home-field advantage over every team in the postseason field except the Brewers, who finished the regular season with the best record in the Majors.
What will the postseason rotation look like?
Yamamoto, Skubal, Snell and Glasnow make up this year's Big Four. The rotation order is yet to be determined. One consideration is that Yamamoto is accustomed to starting on at least five days' rest, whereas the other three are comfortable starting on four days' rest. That makes Yamamoto likely to start Game 1 of the NLDS because he would be available for a potential Game 5 on his normal rest. 
What's the latest on Ohtani's status?
Ohtani was activated from the 15-day IL and hit in the Dodgers' final five games, going 5-for-21 (.238) with eight strikeouts and one walk. Roberts described the performance as Ohtani showing some rust and said the team does not have any health concerns with him. 
Which injured players could return?   
The Dodgers hope that Henriquez, who has emerged as an important leverage arm, can return for the postseason after his regular season came to a premature end due to lower back discomfort. He will face hitters during the bye week, and as long as he comes away feeling good, he will be activated for the NLDS.
Which roster spots may be up for grabs?
The final spot on the bench is far from set in stone. The Dodgers could carry De Paula, but Dalton Rushing, Alex Call and Hyeseong Kim are additional options. This decision could come down to whether they want to use that bench spot on a potential impact bat or someone who brings enhanced speed and/or defense to the table. If L.A. carries fewer than 13 pitchers, that would open an additional bench spot.
The bullpen should also have some openings. If Henriquez does not recover in time for the postseason, that opens an additional spot. Justin Wrobleski, Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan were starters for most of the season, but they will be relief options in the postseason. But Wrobleski was inconsistent in the second half, and the Dodgers have other left-handers who may be more reliable in leverage, such as Bubic.
Who will close out games?
Díaz was supposed to resolve the Dodgers' ninth-inning troubles, but he has only added to them in his first year in L.A. Since returning from the IL, he has looked much better, which could have him back in the mix to close out games. The Dodgers may be more likely to play the matchups instead of going with a set closer in the postseason. Based on regular-season performance, Scott and Henriquez are two of the top options to pitch in save situations. Perhaps Sasaki could reprise his postseason closer role if needed.
